author: westco
quote: For all its technical brilliance, Grand Theft Auto VI feels less like a video game and more like an interactive movie that hates letting you have fun. After waiting over a decade, Rockstar delivered a gorgeous world held back by outdated design and restrictive mechanics.Outdated Mission Design: Despite the modern coat of paint, missions are still painfully linear. Stepping slightly off the designated path or trying a creative approach often triggers an instant "Mission Failed" screen.Style Over Substance: The obsession with realistic physics—like limited weapon carrying and sluggish movement—actively punishes players for trying to cause the classic, over-the-top GTA mayhem.Empty Scale: While Vice City and Leonida look breathtaking, much of the massive map feels like set dressing, lacking meaningful, repeatable activities once the main story wraps up.Anti-Consumer Tactics: Between the 30 FPS console cap, missing PC version, and content locked behind expensive editions, the launch feels engineered to maximize profit rather than player **** short, Rockstar focused so much on making GTA VI look like real life that they forgot to make it play like a great game.
